summary: Intermittent DNS split-horizon caused by UDP proxy translation delaying control-plane heartbeats in private deploy
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports intermittent failures where the private deployment's control-plane heartbeats to Redwood's hosted control plane are delayed by 10-40s and occasionally time out. The symptoms correlate with probe logs showing DNS responses returning the internal split-horizon address for the control-plane endpoint from the customer's UDP-based forwarder, but TCP/HTTPS probes then fail because the forwarder rewrites ephemeral ports and drops EDNS OK flags.

Impact:
- Frostline Health reports degraded model serving on private deployment: occasional model pulls stall and gRPC heartbeat backoffs cause short-lived request latency spikes.
- Affects production workloads in us-east-2; no customer data exfiltration indicated.

Environment:
- Private deployment (VPC peering) with corporate UDP DNS forwarder + on-prem UDP proxy appliance.
- Redwood agent version: 2.11.4 (serving node), control-plane agent: 1.9.0.
- Customer network stack: DNS forwarder -> UDP translation proxy -> egress NAT gateway -> TGW -> Redwood VPCE.

Steps to reproduce (as provided by customer):
1) From serving node, repeatedly resolve control-plane hostname used for agent heartbeat (control.redwood.example).
2) Observe alternating DNS answers: internal A record (10.1.5.12) and public IP (54.210.22.15).
3) When internal A returned, agent attempts TCP/HTTPS to 10.1.5.12 but connection hangs or TLS fails after 15-30s.
4) Heartbeat backoff grows and some in-flight requests see elevated latency; sometimes token refresh fails resulting in transient 401s.

Observed behavior:
- DNS responses from the customer's UDP proxy occasionally strip EDNS0 and set TC=0 (no truncation) causing downstream resolver to believe UDP answer is authoritative; the response includes an internal A record that is routable only inside the customer's CGN.
- The UDP translation appliance rewrites source ports and does asymmetric NAT on the return path which causes TLS session establishment to fail intermittently.

Expected behavior:
- Serving nodes should consistently resolve the public VPCE IP for control plane (or the pinned internal IP when configured), and TCP/TLS sessions should establish within sub-second RTTs.

Temporary workaround provided by customer:
- Customer added a short hostfile override on serving nodes pointing control.redwood.example -> 54.210.22.15 which stabilizes heartbeats but is not sustainable at scale.

Investigation notes (so far):
- Support reproduced DNS answer oscillation using dig +tcp and +udp from a Bastion in us-east-2 behind the customer's forwarder; UDP shows split-horizon internal IP ~1/20 queries.
- Packet captures show UDP proxy rewriting DNS ID and source port and responding with an internal A when a cached internal zone exists; EDNS0 options were stripped in ~70% of UDP responses.
- Control-plane logs show repeated TLS handshake timeouts correlated to the times internal A answers were returned.
- No RBAC/auth failures observed; traffic reaches the customer's network edge and fails before VPCE; no evidence of malicious activity.
- Relevant config on customer's UDP proxy: "translate-udp-encap enable, preserve-udp-id disable, edns-strip enable".

Next steps / proposed remediation:
1) Recommend customer disable EDNS0 stripping on UDP proxy and enable consistent TCP fallback (or lower UDP cache TTL for split-horizon zones).
2) Short-term: customer to roll out hostfile pinning or local forwarder rule on all serving nodes as a stopgap (already tested).
3) Redwood SRE to examine control-plane agent for more aggressive TCP fallback when consecutive UDP answers indicate internal-private IPs and to add additional telemetry to detect split-horizon anomalies.
4) If customer cannot change appliance, propose adding optional agent config to prefer TCP DNS or hardcode VPCE IP via config map during rollout.

Attachments: packet captures (pcap snippets provided by customer), dig traces, agent debug logs (attached).

comments: 2026-03-10 11:02 - Miguel Santos (Support): Initial triage complete. Reproduced split-horizon behavior from customer's bastion. Asking SRE to weigh in on agent-side TCP-DNS fallback. Assigned INT-4021 for SRE investigation.

2026-03-10 15:48 - Priya Menon (SRE): Packet captures reviewed. UDP proxy strips EDNS which can cause downstream UDP caching of internal answers. Suggest customer change proxy config; created internal note about enhancing agent telemetry.
2026-03-11 09:22 - Frostline Network Engineer (Customer): We can disable EDNS strip on the proxy but need a maintenance window. Confirmed hostfile workaround stabilizes the fleet during testing.

2026-03-11 13:06 - Miguel Santos (Support): Documented recommended proxy config and added example iptables-based TCP-only DNS fallback for serving nodes. Scheduling follow-up post-maintenance to verify.
2026-03-12 07:45 - Aisha Kaur (CS): Customer reports maintenance window tomorrow UTC. Requested post-window verification checklist and asked for updated packet captures if issue persists.
workaround: Hostfile override on serving nodes mapping control.redwood.example -> 54.210.22.15; will prevent split-horizon resolution until customer proxy config change is applied.
next_steps: Customer to disable EDNS0 stripping and enable consistent TCP fallback on UDP proxy during maintenance window. Redwood SRE to propose agent change for TCP-preferring DNS when internal IPs are observed, tracked in INT-4021.
